attestations.title: Attestations and graph (Yohualli)
attestations.publishWSSoff: Sign and save locally (queue for relay when gossip connects)
attestations.p2pDesc: Choose <0>WebSocket</0> and a relay URL so other PWAs can receive signatures. <1>BroadcastChannel</1> only shares between tabs of the <2>same origin</2>: if you sign there, after switching to WebSocket and connecting gossip, <3>unsent</3> local signatures are resent. With WSS, the PWA registers interest (your accounts and lab subject); the relay filters; if you publish with no socket, it queues. Buttons below: manual relay and buffer catch-up.
attestations.lead: Local graph in IndexedDB; gossip between tabs (BroadcastChannel) or between PWAs and devices with a WebSocket relay (e.g. <0>relay/</0> on Railway with <1>wss://</1> and the PWA on GitHub Pages with the same URL in <2>VITE_YOHUALLI_RELAY_WS</2>).
attestations.mixedContentError: HTTPS blocks ws://. Click "Proxy /__yohualli_relay" or "Fix: use proxy" and try again to connect.
attestations.optWss: WebSocket relay (other port, other machine, deployed PWA…)
attestations.labelRelayUrl: Relay URL (local ws:// or wss:// in production)

attestations.autoConnectBanner: The app tries to connect to the relay automatically. The URL field and quick presets will appear after 10 seconds, if the connection fails, or you can show them now.

zkLab.title: ZK Lab (Paseo)
zkLab.intro: On-chain verification of the Solidity verifier from Noir / Barretenberg on <0>Polkadot Hub Testnet</0> (EVM, chain ID {{id}}). Contract build and deploy happen in the dev environment (Foundry, etc.), not in the browser.
zkLab.whoBody: Lab page to verify or generate proofs against <0>HonkVerifier</0> / <1>MerkleHonkRegistry</1> (Merkle v1, subject v0, UI samples). It does not replace <2>Attestations</2> (graph and signatures to other identities). Actor map: <3>docs/YOHUALLI_FLUJOS_UX_ACTORES.md</3>.
zkLab.flow1: A Barretenberg proof can be built with nargo + bb prove (or npm run circuit:proof-hex:…) on your dev machine, or in the browser (Prover cards below) for yohualli_subject_commitment_v0 (lighter) and, with limits, yohualli_merkle_attest_v1 (ECDSA, heavy). On-chain verification remains an eth_call to the HonkVerifier for that circuit.
zkLab.flow2: Paste the proof (hex) and public inputs (one bytes32 per line) from the same circuit used to build the on-chain verifier. Use “Load Yohualli sample” to fill embedded proof/inputs, and with VITE_PASEO_VERIFIER_ADDRESS set, the contract address. The “square” sample is another circuit (kusama-noir-lab) and only works with a verifier for that circuit.
zkLab.flow3: The verify call is read-only (eth_call): it does not spend on-chain execution gas. To change state, deploy a wrapper that calls verify and updates storage; this PWA can then sign with the connected EVM wallet.
zkLab.evmDesc: Connect MetaMask or another injected wallet; the PAS for gas on the EVM (revive) layer is shown below (eth_getBalance). The home screen Substrate balance is a different account / ledger and does not replace this.
zkLab.noEthereum: No <0>window.ethereum</0> found. Open the PWA in a browser with a wallet, or the vendor app.
